title: Day 2 of building a story based backrooms game(introducing the characters rough draft) while keeping mechanics out until demo launch video :)
author: Affectionate_Fact854
selftext:
i had this idea in my head inspired by games i loved playing   
Resident evil:biohazard  
F.E.A.R   
and   
watching the backrooms videos 

why not combine the mechanics i loved from each of them   
  
So i have been spending the last 2 days almost no breaks on building the frame work for my attempt at a back rooms game , with a uncovering story plot included 

i used fable and opus.  
heres what i did 

\-Typed out a rough draft of a story /plot i was thinking in my mind of   
\-Punched out all the mechanics of the inspired games above that came to mind that I appreciated   
\-Gave the comp spec requirement   
\-set out the optimization plans i could think of for doing this 

gave fable the document 

we spent 4hours refining each section of the documents , phase plan , mechanics plans   
and took 6 agents to type out the final story, dread events , character traits 

after   
i let fable brows the internet after i told it "with this plan, go find all the assets and potential assets we will need that is cco licensed , make a document of where you got each asset

after   
i had multiple agents in paralle start building each object scene , character scenes,  all the backend managers ,  stress tests , optimization systems and player systems   


where i managed to get after 2 days   
\*floor 1 backroom finished with over 280 unique rooms in a spacial grid   
\*destructible walls the player can break down  
\*flash light with batteries   
\*full floor 1 propped up   
\*enemy system that can detect sounds   
\*player can hide in shadows   
\*over 30 unique notes to read scattered on walls   
\*stable 60fps

Now the biggest chunk is finished   
  
its time to continue building the story of the next 2 backroom floors and    
Building scary dread events while not making use of any gore factors

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: I must finally be on the opposite side of what is hip and cool because I find the backrooms to be a very bland and boring concept. In some ways, even a lazy excuse to put in no effort since "yeah it's the backrooms it's supposed to just be empty basic box rooms with the same 3 textures!"
